title: Progressive Wages and the Revaluing of "Low-wage Work"
what_it_is: Progressive Wages and the Revaluing of "Low-wage Work"

sections.label: PWM sectors and workers
sections.summary: PWMs cover seven sectors and two occupations and have significantly improved wages of over 150,000 workers, or 50% of low-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas
sentences.text: PWMs have been implemented in seven sectors and for two occupations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas
sentences.text: The PWMs have significantly improved the wages of over 150,000 workers or 50% of low-wage workers.

sections.label: Sunday Times survey findings
sections.summary: A 2020 Sunday Times survey found 78% of respondents would pay more for essential workers, and 55% would pay at least 20% more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas
sentences.text: A 2020 Sunday Times survey found that 78% of respondents were willing to pay more for essential workers, such as cleaners and security officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas
sentences.text: Even better, they were willing to do so if the extra amount went to the workers themselves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas
sentences.text: And 55% were willing to pay at least 20% more.

sections.label: PWM wage growth statistics
sections.summary: Statistics show PWMs have significantly increased wage growth in the respective sectors and the placing of a monetary value on work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas
sentences.text: Second, statistics show that the PWMs have significantly increased growth in wages in the respective sectors and therefore of the placing of a particular monetary value on work.

sections.label: Security officer minimum wages
sections.summary: Basic-level security officers must earn a minimum of $2,650 today, rising to over $3,500 by 2028.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas
sentences.text: Today, security officers at the basic level must earn a minimum of $2,650, and by 2028, their minimum wage will grow to over $3,500.

sections.label: PWM revaluing low-wage work
sections.summary: The PWMs have contributed to the revaluing of low-wage work, but this is just the beginning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas
sentences.text: In the round, the PWMs have undoubtedly contributed to the revaluing of low-wage work, but this is just the beginning.

sections.label: Easing sectors out of PWM
sections.summary: Zaqy Mohamad entertained easing sectors out of the PWM, though there are no plans yet, and sectoral PWMs must eventually return wage increases to the market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas
sentences.text: Indeed, in this weekend's Straits Times article, Senior Minister of State Zaqy Mohamad had entertained the possibility of sectors being eased out of the PWM, although there are no plans to do so as yet.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas
sentences.text: Sectoral PWMs, once they have achieved their objective of correcting wages that were valued wrongly must at some point return the determination of wage increases to the market.

sections.label: Vulnerable workers remaining vulnerable
sections.summary: Failure to act means vulnerable workers will remain vulnerable forever.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas
sentences.text: If we fail to do so, then these vulnerable workers will remain vulnerable forever.

sections.label: Reviewing non-PWM employee wages
sections.summary: Companies in PWM sectors must review non-PWM employees' wages to ensure they are commensurate with PWM wage increases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas
sentences.text: Companies in PWM sectors will also have to review the wages of their non-PWM employees and to ensure they are commensurate with the increases of the wages of PWM-covered sectors.

sections.label: Sectoral clusters and wage floors
sections.summary: Sectoral tripartite clusters would no longer prescribe year-on-year wage increases, and prevailing wage floors would continue as sectoral minimum wages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas
sentences.text: First, the respective sectoral tripartite clusters would no longer need to prescribe year-on-year wage increases over a period of a few years, which is the current practice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas
sentences.text: The prevailing wage floors at the point of moving to 2.0 would continue to apply and to be enforced as a form of sectoral minimum wage for each rung.

sections.label: AI Literacy Programme for security professionals
sections.summary: Certis and SUTD's AI Literacy Programme, launched by Minister of State Gan Siow Huang, aims to upskill 5,000 security professionals by 2027.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas
sentences.text: The AI Literacy Programme designed by Certis and the Singapore University of Technology and Design was launched by Minister of State Gan Siow Huang last week and aims to upskill 5,000 security professionals with AI knowledge by 2027.

sections.label: Tripartite partners stepping in again
sections.summary: If PWM 2.0 sector wages stagnate after returning to the market, tripartite partners can step in again to prescribe wage increases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas
sentences.text: If wages in a PWM 2.0 sector stagnate for some time after they are returned to the market, then the tripartite partners can step in again to prescribe wage increases.

sections.label: Conclusion on PWMs
sections.summary: PWMs have raised wages and skills, and as they mature beyond their 10th year they will continue to raise wages and improve workers' conditions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas
sentences.text: To conclude, Sir, the PWMs have raised wages and skills in their respective sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas
sentences.text: This has contributed to the enhancement of the value of the work in each sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas
sentences.text: As the PWMs mature beyond their 10th year, I am confident that we will continue to position the PWMs to raise wages, increase productivity, to improve the working conditions of our workers and to contribute to their sense of dignity and pride in their work.

sections.label: PWM wage growth outcomes
sections.summary: Tripartite partners started mandatory PWM in cleaning in 2014, then landscape and security in 2016; local wages in these sectors grew 31% from 2014 to 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Tripartite partners implemented the first mandatory PWM in 2014 in the cleaning sector, followed by landscape and security in 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Real cumulative wage growth of locals in these initial PWM sectors grew by 31% from 2014 to 2019, outpacing wage growth of the 20th percentile (P20) worker at 23%.

sections.label: Entry-level cleaner wage increase
sections.summary: The basic wage requirement for entry-level cleaners will rise from $1,312 in 2022 to $2,420 in 2028.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: For example, the basic wage requirement for entry-level cleaners will increase from $1,312 back in 2022 to $2,420 in 2028.

sections.label: Entry-level security officer wages
sections.summary: By 2028, entry-level security officers will earn at least $3,530.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: By 2028, entry-level security officers will earn at least $3,530.

sections.label: Government payouts to employers
sections.summary: The Government disbursed around $1 billion to 70,000 employers who gave wage increases to more than 345,000 employees in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: The Government disbursed around $1 billion to 70,000 employers who gave wage increases to more than 345,000 employees in 2022.

sections.label: Outcome-based contracting practices
sections.summary: Tripartite partners have been promoting good industry practices among service buyers, such as outcome-based contracting specifying clear deliverables rather than number of workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Tripartite partners have been promulgating good industry practices among service buyers, such as outcome-based contracting to specify clear deliverables in a contract, rather than the number of workers.

sections.label: PWM flexibility and market forces
sections.summary: The PWM currently allows some flexibility for market forces, with retail and food services roles like retail managers and senior cooks in the PWM ladder but not wage-mandated.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Currently, there is some flexibility in the PWM for market forces to play a role.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Examples are the retail and food services sectors, where jobs such as retail managers and senior cooks are part of the PWM ladder, but their wages are not mandated by PWM.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: As PWM sectors negotiate wage requirements over the next few years, we hope that more workers can see significant uplift and over time, more higher-level job roles can have their wages left to market forces.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: But for now, the majority of our PWM workers still need the support and uplift from our PWM requirements.

sections.label: Implementing PWMs effectively
sections.summary: With wages coverage extended, efforts to implement PWMs effectively must be doubled down on.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: For now, having extended the coverage of our wages, we must double down on our efforts to implement our PWMs effectively.
